title: Release notes pipeline experiment: model changelog generator approaches (staging)
content:
Purpose
- Compare candidate generation approaches for customer-visible model changelog entries.
- Measure: failure rates, publish latency, and manual editing burden.
- Environment: staging only, using migrated + synthetic change-events.

Definitions / notes
- “Entry” = one customer-visible changelog item produced from one or more underlying model metadata change-events.
- “Failure” = pipeline produced no publishable entry without human intervention (blocked in validation, template rendering error, publish job failure, or policy/redaction violation).
- Manual edits counted when a human changes generated customer_safe_summary or required sections before approval.
- Publish latency measured from change-event ingestion timestamp to docs publish completion (or console availability if docs step skipped).
- Time window: 2026-01-27 to 2026-02-11 (11 business days).

Table 1 — Experiment matrix (high level)
| Experiment ID | Name | Source of truth | Grouping strategy | Publish targets | Review workflow | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EXP-A | Git-tag/docs-driven notes | Git tags + docs PRs | per release train | Docs only | Docs PR review | Rejected (doesn’t cover Dedicated/Private + poor audit story) |
| EXP-B | Registry events (naive) | Model registry change-events | group by model_id + calendar day | Docs + Console | draft -> published | Iterated (see EXP-C) |
| EXP-C | Registry events (deterministic + policy) | Model registry change-events (signed) | group by model_id + ordered by event_id; “no-merge if >1 distinct change_type” | Docs + Console + feed | draft -> in_review -> published + RBAC | Current baseline |
| EXP-D | Hybrid (registry event + runtime release note link) | Registry + runtime release note metadata | same as EXP-C | Docs + Console | draft -> in_review -> published | Partial (needs runtime linking rules) |

Table 2 — Results summary
| Metric | EXP-A: Git/docs | EXP-B: Registry naive | EXP-C: Registry deterministic | EXP-D: Hybrid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Entries attempted (n) | 42 | 96 | 112 | 28 |
| Auto-published w/o human changes | 38% (16/42) | 41% (39/96) | 62% (69/112) | 57% (16/28) |
| Manual edits required (any) | 62% | 59% | 38% | 43% |
| Median manual edit time per edited entry | 6 min | 9 min | 5 min | 7 min |
| Failure rate (blocked) | 7% | 12% | 4% | 11% |
| Median publish latency | 18h 22m | 2h 14m | 2h 41m | 3h 08m |
| P95 publish latency | 42h 10m | 11h 55m | 9h 12m | 15h 40m |
| Docs publish job failures (count) | 1 | 6 | 2 | 3 |
| Policy/redaction violations caught pre-publish | 0 (but relies on manual discipline) | 8 | 3 | 4 |
| Broken links detected post-publish (spot check) | 3 | 5 | 1 | 2 |

Table 3 — Failure modes (counts)
| Failure mode | EXP-A | EXP-B | EXP-C | EXP-D | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Schema validation error (missing required fields) | 0 | 5 | 2 | 2 | Mostly deprecation fields + compatibility matrix gaps during backfill |
| Template render error | 0 | 2 | 1 | 1 | One case: null “replacement_model” referenced in deprecation section |
| Grouping bug (incorrectly collapsed multiple updates) | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 | Fixed by deterministic ordering by event_id (see PR-18944) |
| Docs publish job failed (build/deploy) | 1 | 6 | 2 | 3 | Includes one staging incident: docs link 404 due to deploy ordering |
| Redaction/policy violation | 0 | 2 | 1 | 2 | Internal model nickname leaked in provenance.vendor_details in two early drafts |
| Approval workflow blocked (missing approver / RBAC) | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | One entry stuck in in_review due to role mismatch in staging |

Table 4 — Manual edit categories (percent of edited entries)
| Edit category | EXP-A | EXP-B | EXP-C | EXP-D | Examples |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Wording/clarity (customer_safe_summary) | 54% | 61% | 49% | 58% | “kernel change” -> “performance optimizations”; removing internal acronyms |
| Missing compatibility notes | 12% | 28% | 9% | 11% | Context window change without explicit “no action required” line |
| Incorrect change type tagging | 9% | 17% | 6% | 7% | “perf” vs “behavior” vs “compatibility” |
| Deprecation timeline formatting | 3% | 14% | 5% | 9% | Sunset date present but message missing replacement guidance |
| Links to evals/dashboards | 31% | 22% | 18% | 25% | In v1 we only link; still had missing link placeholders |
| Security/policy phrasing | 5% | 9% | 4% | 6% | Avoiding claims like “guaranteed safe”; using approved language |

Table 5 — Latency breakdown (EXP-C only)
| Stage | Median | P95 | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Event ingestion -> draft rendered | 3m 40s | 14m 05s | Worker queue depth spikes correlate with other batch jobs |
| Draft rendered -> moved to in_review | 1h 12m | 6h 30m | Driven by human review SLAs; most delays during end-of-day |
| In_review -> approved/published | 52m | 3h 10m | Most approvals happen in clusters after PM/Docs office hours |
| Publish -> docs available | 12m | 55m | Docs build + cache invalidation; RSS generation adds ~2m |

Qualitative notes / takeaways
- EXP-A (git/docs) is too slow and too manual; also fails the “single source of truth” requirement and doesn’t map cleanly to Dedicated/Private rollouts.
- EXP-B validated the event-driven direction but had a major issue: collapsing multiple updates in a day created misleading summaries. Deterministic ordering + stricter grouping rules reduced confusion.
- EXP-C is the best current baseline: lowest failure rate and lowest manual edit time; still needs better default copy for compatibility sections.
- EXP-D adds value by cross-linking runtime notes but increases failure surface area. Recommendation: keep runtime linking as optional enrichment (non-blocking) for v1.

Recommendations (Release Eng)
1) Adopt EXP-C as v1 implementation baseline.
2) Enforce “no-merge if multiple distinct change_types for same model/version within 24h” unless explicitly overridden (prevents confusing combined entries).
3) Treat docs publish as retriable + non-blocking for console availability (console can show published entry even if docs lag, but must display docs_sync_status).
4) Add a pre-approval checklist in the UI for: compatibility section present, deprecation timeline present if applicable, and no internal-only fields.

Open questions
- Do we want a hard SLA for publish latency, or only for review queue time? (Currently biggest contributor to P95 is human review.)
- What’s the policy for “behavior change” entries when we don’t have eval diffs integrated (v1 non-goal)?
- For hotfix corrections: do we auto-generate a “superseded by” entry or require an explicit editor-authored correction note every time?

Action items
- Connor O’Brien: align generator publish schedule with release freeze windows (draft is OK during freeze; publish needs explicit override). (due 2026-02-20)
- Michael Nguyen: tighten validation for deprecation fields (replacement required when sunset_date is set). (tracked in ENG-4924 follow-up)
- Elliot Price / Wei Chen: update template copy to always include a plain-language “Impact” sentence even for perf-only changes. (docs style guide follow-up)
- Logan Wright: add metrics for review queue age + percent entries requiring manual edits, broken down by change_type. (ENG-4930)

Change log
- 2026-02-13: Updated EXP-C results after deterministic ordering fix (PR-18944) rerun; reduced failures and removed grouping bug category for EXP-C.
- 2026-02-07: Added manual edit category breakdown + latency stage breakdown.
- 2026-01-24: Initial matrix drafted after first staging run.
